title: Tor bounds detected on pro-etale covers and open-closed decompositions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For integers $c\leq d$, say that a complex has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ when its derived tensor with every module sheaf in degree zero has zero cohomology outside $[c,d]$; use K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$ use the inverse-image ring $f^{-1}A$ and module inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. (i) If $\{V_i\to X\}$ is a pro-étale covering family and every $K|_{V_i}$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. (ii) If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion], and $i^{-1}K,j^{-1}K$ have Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. No quasi-coherence, Noetherian or finite-cover hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, put $A_Y=f^{-1}A$ and give the induced morphism of topoi the identity structural map $f^{-1}A\to A_Y$. The transported module inverse image $F_f:\operatorname{Mod}(A)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y)$ is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives its unbounded derived functor by applying $F_f$ termwise, and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies this functor with $Lf^*$. We denote it by $f^{-1}$, consistently with the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], for any complex representative of $E\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ and every integer $q$,
$$H^q(f^{-1}E)\cong f^{-1}H^q(E).$$
This holds for unbounded $E$, and $f^{-1}(M[0])=(f^{-1}M)[0]$ for any module sheaf $M$.

source.place: Tag 04JC (lemma-flat-pullback-exact), with derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor) and homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this morphism of ringed topoi with source coefficient ring $f^{-1}A$. Its tensor comparison, together with step 1, gives, for every $A$-module sheaf $M$,
$$f^{-1}(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0])\cong(f^{-1}K)\otimes_{f^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(f^{-1}M)[0].$$
Here the theorem applies to arbitrary unbounded complexes and arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings on the chosen small sites. The structural ring map is the identity, so the pullback is precisely the transported inverse image of step 1; no flatness assertion about a change to a different coefficient ring is needed.

For (i), fix an arbitrary $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q\notin[c,d]$, and set $F=H^q(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0])$. For $u_i:V_i\to X$, steps 1 and 2 identify $u_i^{-1}F$ with $H^q((u_i^{-1}K)\otimes_{u_i^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(u_i^{-1}M)[0])$, which vanishes by the assumed Tor bound. The abelian-sheaf clause of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] identifies the underlying $u_i^{-1}F$ with slice restriction $F|_{V_i}$; that clause applies to every abelian sheaf (one may instantiate its unused constant ring parameter with $\mathbf Z$), without restricting the coefficient sheaf $A$. For each site object $W$, the pullbacks $W\times_XV_i\to W$ form a covering by the pullback axiom for the site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and their domains map to the $V_i$. Thus the family of slice restrictions satisfies the covering-sieve hypothesis of [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]. Apply that lemma to the underlying abelian-sheaf map $F\to0$: every restriction is an isomorphism since $F|_{V_i}=0$. It follows that $F=0$ as an abelian sheaf and therefore as an $A$-module sheaf (the zero abelian sheaf has a unique module action). Since $M$ and $q$ were arbitrary, this proves (i).

source.place: Tags 03CE (lemma-localize-given-products) and 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps); covering base change in the site axioms

proof.text:
For (ii), fix any $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q\notin[c,d]$ and again put $F=H^q(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0])$. Steps 1 and 2, first with $f=i$ and then with $f=j$, give
$$i^{-1}F\cong H^q((i^{-1}K)\otimes_{i^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(i^{-1}M)[0])=0,\qquad
j^{-1}F\cong H^q((j^{-1}K)\otimes_{j^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(j^{-1}M)[0])=0.$$
The equalities are exactly the two assumed Tor bounds, tested on the module sheaves $i^{-1}M$ and $j^{-1}M$. Now [lem-exc-open-closed-detection] applies to $F$ with $R_X=A$, $R_Z=i^{-1}A$, $R_U=j^{-1}A$ and the identity coefficient identifications. Its hypotheses are the given closed immersion and complementary quasi-compact open immersion; it allows an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings. It gives $F=0$. Varying $M$ and $q$ proves (ii), with precisely the same interval $[c,d]$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q28-c64b9e8b8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item's four steps and all nine cited statements, plus the ancestor's Locality and Strata paragraphs (main-20261015 ctf-equals-bc.proof.md lines 18-30). No new nodes, no repair note, item not on the 2026-10-19 drop list, no SGA source. Step 1 is correct: f_proet is a geometric morphism via lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor, so the module inverse image is exact (lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact), and the termwise derived functor is a left derived functor, hence equal to Lu^*. Step 2 is correct: the ringed-topoi tensor pullback with S=u^{-1}R and the identity ring map gives u^*=u^{-1}. Step 3 is correct: the abelian clause of object inverse image = slice restriction, cover base change gives the CoversTop condition, then Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop applied to F->0. Step 4 is correct: lem-exc-open-closed-detection (arbitrary R_X, j quasi-compact) is applied to F=H^q(K⊗^L M), with the bounds tested on i^{-1}M and j^{-1}M. Edge cases checked: empty X and empty cover, Z or U empty, c=d, F_ℓ over Z/ℓ². No cycle, and no duplicate (lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction is the converse direction). Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact accepted: it is generic exactness of inverse image along any geometric morphism, its closure contains only two general trf definitions (def-trf-geometric-morphism, def-trf-abelian-inverse-image-presentation), and the batch-5 targets already reach it without this item through weil-pbc nodes. lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact could replace it, but that is optional.
